newsitem.title: USA: GM 1996 profit sharing checks fall.
newsitem.headline: GM 1996 profit sharing checks fall.

text.p: General Motors Corp's U.S. represented employees will receive average 1996 profit sharing checks of $300, the automaker said Tuesday, less than half of the $800 they received for 1995.

The checks will be sent to 282,000 represented employees in the U.S. who worked full-time for the year. In addition, GM said 76,000 eligible salaried workers will receive 1996 incentive payments under a salaried program, with payments rising with the level of pay and responsibility.
GM reported 1996 operating earnings of $5.0 billion, compared to $6.0 billion for 1995.
Last week, Chrysler Corp said it will pay its U.S. workers an average of $7,900 for 1996 profit sharing.

GM said average retail incentives for its North American Operations in the fourth quarter were $739 a vehicle, up from $518 a year ago. For Europe, the average incentive was $580, compared to $326 in the 1995 fourth quarter.

Fourth quarter car inventories in the U.S. were 93 days supply, down from 103 a year ago. Trucks rose to 97 days supply from 81. The percentage of fourth quarter sales that went to fleet dealers fell to 17.2 percent from 19.5 percent.
GM's combined car and truck market share in the U.S. fell to 30.2 percent in the fourth quarter from 33.5 percent a year ago. Unit deliveries in the U.S. were 1,085,000, down from 1,205,000.
Capacity utilization for the quarter in the U.S. and Canada, based on two shifts a day, was 79.9 percent, down from 85.2 percent in the 1995 fourth period.
Worldwide unit deliveries in the quarter fell to 1,923,000 from 2,019,000. That gave GM a worldwide market share of 15.5 percent, down from 17.3 percent in the 1995 fourth quarter.
